blocking.section: Decision outcome (Local bucket, State Store failure and Fail-open bound rows; Figure 1) and Consequences
blocking.issue: The fail-open bound cannot hold with the local bucket the ADR describes. A token bucket whose capacity and refill both equal the per-Node ceiling admits up to its full capacity at once, then another ceiling's worth of refill within the same window: up to 2 × ceiling per Node per window. So while the State Store fails, a key can get up to 2 × N × ceiling per window, not N × ceiling. The ADR itself counts GCRA's τ = window as 2 × `requests`, but it treats the bucket as if it had no burst. The owning document closes this gap only for derived ceilings: 'while GCRA fails each derived-ceiling bucket holds ... tokens per epoch-aligned window, without carry-over'. The ADR leaves that rule out. The same factor of 2 applies to the untagged State Store call bound in Consequences.
blocking.evidence: Local bucket row: "One token bucket per key and `limits[]` entry at the per-Node ceiling". State Store failure row: "`open` (default) admits within the local buckets". Fail-open bound row: "At most N × per-Node ceiling per key per window, N being serving Nodes (target)". Consequences: "a key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, N × ceiling) times per window". Owning document, Per-Node ceiling: "while GCRA fails each derived-ceiling bucket holds max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) tokens per epoch-aligned window, without carry-over"; decision path figure: "Admit from unfloored local buckets (target)".
blocking.fix: Change the State Store failure row to: "A failed or timed-out call, or an open State client breaker, applies `failureMode`: `open` (default) admits from the local buckets, which while calls fail refill once per epoch-aligned `window` without carry-over; `closed` returns 503 `RZ-STS-<NNN>`". Relabel Figure 1's `ok2` node "Admit from aligned-window local buckets". In Consequences, change the bound to "at most min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) times per window (target), a bucket's capacity plus its refill". Keep the total length at or under 1,500 words (the body has 1,490 now) by cutting duplicated text, for example ", the cached form of `EVAL`," in the GCRA row. Also list the aligned-window refill for declared ceilings as a pack 8.8 amendment in More information.

blocking.section: Decision drivers (Hot-key protection), Decision outcome rationale, Consequences and Confirmation (CE-12, CE-15)
blocking.issue: The chosen option does not meet the Hot-key protection driver for keys spread across many Nodes, and the ADR claims it does. Each locally admitted request runs GCRA. A busy constant key, such as a service limit, spread across N Nodes therefore sends up to N × ceiling (about the full limit) script calls per window to one shard. At 1,000,000 requests per second, that is 10 times the roughly 100,000 calls per second the ADR itself assumes a shard can serve. Every Node's breaker for that shard then opens, and co-tenant keys fall to `failureMode`. The owning document and Scalability and distributed state say such keys MUST use `localOnly`, which exists only as a proposal (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (c), OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11). Confirmation cites CE-12, which checks that result through `localOnly`, and CE-15, which checks a first-seen budget. Under option (c), the conforming behavior this ADR follows, neither mechanism exists.
blocking.evidence: Decision drivers: "**Hot-key protection**: one busy key must not starve its shard's co-tenants." Decision outcome: "the local bucket answers most denials and shields shards without a round trip". Consequences: "so a pinned abusive client never loads a shard". Confirmation: "CE-12 and CE-15 ... hot keys and key floods stay within their bounds". Scalability and distributed state, Hot keys: "A key whose `requests` exceed 25% of one shard's calls, about 25,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use `localOnly` mode"; CE-12: "then above it as `localOnly` (hypothesis) | ... no co-tenant breaker opens". Owning document Failure matrix: "above about 100,000 per second (hypothesis) every Node's shard breaker opens and co-tenants apply `failureMode`".
blocking.fix: Add a Consequences bullet: "Bad, because a key spread over many Nodes and admitted above about 25,000 per second (hypothesis) runs GCRA on one shard for every request; until OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 adds `localOnly`, it can open every Node's breaker for that shard's co-tenants." Narrow the driver or the rationale to "shields shards from denied and pinned traffic". In Confirmation, say that CE-12 and CE-15 verify the proposed amendments in OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11. For the conforming design, confirm with CE-3, CE-4 and CE-5 plus an integration check that a hot key over the shard hypothesis opens the breaker and co-tenants apply `failureMode`. Make the change word-neutral, for example by merging the "Nodes stay disposable" Good bullet into the No coordination driver.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (One round trip and Code rows)
blocking.issue: The NOSCRIPT behavior contradicts a depends_on document, and the library helper most implementers would reach for breaks it. The tech stack Library catalog row, which the ADR cites in Confirmation, specifies "`EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback". The conventional reading, and what rueidis's `Lua.Exec` helper does, is to retry with `EVAL` when `EVALSHA` returns NOSCRIPT. That retry is a second blocking round trip in the same request and breaks pack 8.7 rule 1. The ADR says only "Ruralz scripts over rueidis" and does not forbid that helper. It also does not reconcile its rule with the catalog wording. Two sources then disagree about the request-path round-trip count.
blocking.evidence: One round trip row: "`NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and schedules a reload, never a second call (pack section 8.7 rule 1)". Code row: "Ruralz scripts over rueidis ([source](https://github.com/redis/rueidis))". docs/engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md Library catalog: "`EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback".
blocking.fix: Change the Code row to: "Ruralz scripts sent as raw `EVALSHA` through rueidis `Do`, never `Lua.Exec`, whose `EVAL` retry on `NOSCRIPT` is a second round trip; the reload is single-flight per shard". In More information, add that the Library catalog's "`NOSCRIPT` fallback" means this `failureMode` path, and list it as a tech stack correction. Keep the change word-neutral by dropping "; redis_rate is bound to go-redis and not linked": the catalog row and the Dependency admission bullet in Confirmation already cover it.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Local bucket and Over-limit cache rows)
blocking.issue: Per-Node state has no memory bound. The rules create one token bucket per key per `limits[]` entry and one over-limit entry per denied key. Keys come from CEL over client input such as `source.ip`, so cardinality is attacker-controlled. The ADR states no cap, no eviction and no accounting for what eviction costs. An evicted bucket restarts full, which is an extra ceiling per eviction. An implementation built from this ADR alone grows these maps without limit under a key-rotation flood. The owning document bounds them, and the ADR is silent.
blocking.evidence: Local bucket row: "One token bucket per key and `limits[]` entry at the per-Node ceiling". Over-limit cache row: "A key GCRA denied stays denied locally until its retry-after". Owning document, Decision path: "Buckets, local-only and over-limit entries share a Node-wide 1,048,576 entries, about 64 MiB (target), in [Data plane](03-data-plane.md)'s CLOCK-evicted shards, surviving Hot Reloads." Scalability and distributed state: "Rate Limit | Node restart | At most one extra ceiling per key per restarted Node (target)".
blocking.fix: Add a row: "Local state | Buckets and over-limit entries share Data plane's Node-wide, CLOCK-evicted table of 1,048,576 entries, about 64 MiB (target), and survive Hot Reload; an evicted bucket restarts full, adding at most one ceiling per eviction, and GCRA still bounds the Cell". Offset the words elsewhere, for example by shortening Considered option 6 to "**Local bucket plus GCRA, fail-closed by default**, like Envoy's `failure_mode_deny: true` ([source](...))", which also makes its label match its H3.

non_blocking.section: Pros and cons of the options (Local limits only; Local bucket plus GCRA, fail-open)
non_blocking.suggestion: Option 3 is rejected partly because Tyk's DRL is "unreliable at low rate limits where requests are not fairly balanced". With pack 8.8's limit / N ceiling, the chosen option has the same weakness: local buckets deny an unevenly spread key before GCRA would. With an accurate count and balanced load, the sum of the ceilings equals the limit, so the per-request GCRA call binds only when the count lags, in file mode, or with declared or headroom ceilings. State this in the chosen option's Bad bullet, and tie it to OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-16 so the comparison is fair.

The owning document gives a Control-mode Node without a count a fail-open clamp of max(1, `requests` / 100) and the degraded reason `node_count_unknown`. The ADR says only "with neither, as in file mode, the full limit". Either mention the clamp or point to the owning document's Per-Node ceiling section, so no reader applies N × limit to Control-mode Nodes restarted during a Ruralz Control outage.

Say how scripts reach every primary in cluster mode, for example `SCRIPT LOAD` to each node rueidis lists. Scripts are not replicated to replicas, so failover is detected only through `NOSCRIPT`. Under `failureMode: closed`, each Node × shard then returns 503 `RZ-STS-002` until its single-flight reload completes. Bound that burst, or accept it as a Bad consequence.

A hot key on one Node puts every goroutine that serves it on one bucket. Specify a lock-free CAS update or per-shard striping, and add a contention benchmark to Confirmation (Performance budgets and benchmarking owns the figure).

No research file shows that a script can call `TIME` before writes (effects replication) on Redis 8, Valkey and Dragonfly, or how Dragonfly's declared-keys rule applies. Add a research row, or add an Open question in the owning document, before M1. Also note that a failover to a replica with a skewed clock shifts TATs.
"the hybrid Envoy recommends" goes further than the research quote ("can be used in conjunction with global rate limiting to reduce load"). Write "the hybrid Envoy documents".
Because `<requests>/<window>` is part of the key, changing a limit starts fresh GCRA state and briefly allows 2 × limit. The owning document says so, and the ADR should add it as a Bad consequence.
